reasons.plausibility: Introducing pores into a dense alloy inherently reduces load-bearing cross-section and creates stress concentrations, making it highly unlikely to maintain strength and toughness, especially at 1000 °C where creep and oxidation are exacerbated by porosity.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and feasible, with a well-defined falsification criterion based on comparing mechanical properties of porous vs. as-cast samples.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it proposes a method (adding porosity) that is fundamentally detrimental to mechanical properties, contradicting the core goal of maintaining strength while reducing density.
